column1: # India SMS sender IDs (TRAI "headers"): structure, suffix meaning and a short list of verified brand headers.
# Tab separated. First column is the record type. Lines starting with # are comments.
# Maintainer notes are in docs/INDIA_SENDER_IDS.md. Add a header only with a public source you can cite in SRC.
# SRC  key  url  accessed  what it supports
# OAP  X  operator              first letter of the 2-letter prefix (originating access provider)
# LSA  Y  circle                second letter of the prefix (licence service area)
# SUF  letter  KIND  meaning    suffix added by the access provider (TRAI 2nd amendment 2025)
# HDR  header  CATEGORY  brand  src-key   exact 6-character header (without prefix and suffix)
# ENDS text  CATEGORY  src-key  heuristic: a header ending in this text (not a brand claim)

column5: Header = XY-ABCDEF; X operator, Y circle; six alphanumeric characters (TRAI, 16 Jun 2020)
Suffix -P -S -T -G for promotional, service, transactional, government (TCCCPR Second Amendment Regulations 2025, 12 Feb 2025)
HDFC Bank security page: SMS "will always include a header like HDFCBK / HDFCBN" (read from a search excerpt; the page itself redirected and was not opened)
SBI YONO page: legitimate SMS headers SBIINB, SBIPSG or SBICRD (read from a search excerpt)
Axis Bank fraud-awareness pages name AXISBK and AXISMR as its SMS senders (read from search excerpts; AXISMR is shown as promotional, AXISMR-P, in the bank's RBI notice booklet)
Consumer article listing VM-SBIINB, BV-SBIPSG, VM-SBIPSG, BZ-CBSSBI as SBI headers
Trade press examples of suffixed headers: VM-BLUDRT-S (Blue Dart), KA-ZOMATO-S (Zomato), GJ-MEESHO-P (Meesho)
Not a brand claim: a header that ends in these letters usually names a bank or a UPI service. Weak evidence only.
